properties.Name: Maine
properties.Note: Admitted as a free state under the Missouri Compromise of 1820.

properties.Name: New Jersey
properties.Basis: An 1846 law abolished slavery here but kept the last enslaved people bound to their owners as 'apprentices'. The 1850 census still counted 236 people as enslaved.

properties.Name: California
properties.Basis: Admitted as a free state on September 9, 1850, as part of the Compromise of 1850.

properties.Name: Virginia
properties.Note: Includes today's West Virginia, which was part of Virginia until 1863.

properties.Name: Texas
properties.Note: Annexed as a slave state in 1845.

properties.Name: Missouri
properties.Note: Admitted as a slave state under the Missouri Compromise of 1820, although almost all of it lies north of the compromise line. The source map draws the northwest corner, added in 1837, separately; here it is part of the state.

properties.Name: District of Columbia
properties.Basis: Slavery was legal here. A law in the Compromise of 1850 banned bringing enslaved people into the District to sell them, starting January 1, 1851. It did not end slavery here.

properties.Name: Minnesota Territory
properties.Basis: Organized in 1849. Slavery was banned here.

properties.Name: Unorganized territory
properties.Basis: Closed to slavery by the Missouri Compromise of 1820, because it lies north of the compromise line.

properties.Name: Utah Territory
properties.Basis: Organized by the Compromise of 1850, which left slavery for the settlers to decide.
properties.Note: Includes a small area on its eastern edge that the source map draws separately: land north of the Missouri Compromise line that the 1850 act placed in Utah Territory.

properties.Name: New Mexico Territory
properties.Basis: Organized by the Compromise of 1850, which left slavery for the settlers to decide.

properties.Name: Indian Territory
properties.Basis: Not an organized territory. Slavery was legal among several of the nations moved here in the 1830s.

properties.Name: Unorganized land given up by Texas
properties.Basis: Claimed by Texas until 1850. The 1845 resolution that annexed Texas barred slavery in its land north of the Missouri Compromise line. In 1850 it was left outside any organized territory.
